goal: `mc vault unlock` on macOS stores its durable key cache again, so later processes — headless ones included — read the vault without a prompt, and cache entries written before 2026-10-10 keep reading.

A Memoro token the server rejects (expired after its 90 days, or revoked) no longer strands `mc vault`: at a terminal mc deletes the dead token and runs the device flow; anywhere else it fails with a message naming the command that signs in. No sign-in hint in mc names a command that does not exist.
contract: `macSet`'s refusal of a double quote, a backslash or a line break (`src/lib/keychain.js`, `EBADSECRET`) stays exactly as it is, and `setSecret` keeps rethrowing `EBADSECRET` instead of falling back to the file. The cache adapts to the keychain, not the other way round.
A vault key cache entry written before this project — plain JSON in the keychain entry `mc-vault:active-key` — keeps reading as before.
The Memoro server, the device token's lifetime and the device flow's own steps are unchanged; nothing in the memoro repository is touched.
No new verb and no new flag. Signing in stays the device flow that `src/bin-mc.js` runs for `mc vault <verb>` at a terminal.

A rejected token is deleted only in a run that then starts the device flow: interactive (stdout is a TTY), not `--json`, no `MEMORO_TOKEN` in the environment, `MC_TEST_MODE` not `1`. Every other run leaves the keychain as it found it.
Every step runs `npm test` and lands through `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.
out_of_scope: The `OAUTH_STALE` instructions of `mc vault destroy-forgotten` (`src/cli/vault.js` ~1335–1347), which name `mc auth logout` and `mc auth status`. Whether a token from the device flow satisfies the server's fresh-authentication check there is not known, so that text is not rewritten here.

Vault API callers outside `mc vault` — `src/vault/engine/c1-claude-lease.js`, `src/vault/credential-domain/local-codex.js`, `src/adapters/managed-runtime/claude-managed-custody.js`. They will see the new `err.code` on a rejected token but keep their own handling.
Bare `mc` (the page, `src/mc/commands/home.js`) signing in. It does not run the device flow today and does not start to.
A headless session signing in by itself.

success_criteria.criterion: The vault key cache is written through the real macOS keychain guard and read back.
success_criteria.check: `tests/vault/engine/key-cache.test.js`: `cacheVaultKey` with `deps.setSecret` calling the real `macSet` (only its `exec` stubbed, capturing the `security -i` stdin line) returns `true`, and `readCachedVaultKey` with `deps.getSecret` returning the captured `-w` value yields the same 32 key bytes, `durable: true`, and the `authHash` and `deviceId` that were written.

success_criteria.criterion: A cache entry in the pre-2026-10-10 shape still reads, and a corrupt encoded entry is cleared rather than thrown.
success_criteria.check: `tests/vault/engine/key-cache.test.js`: a store seeded with `JSON.stringify({ vaultKeyB64, authHash, expiresAt: null })` reads as present and is not deleted; a store seeded with `b64:` followed by non-base64 or non-JSON reads as `null`, `inspectCachedVaultKey` reports `invalid-json`, and the entry is deleted.

success_criteria.criterion: Only the server's token rejection is classed as a rejected token; a wrong master password is not.
success_criteria.check: `tests/lib/api.test.js`: a 401 with body `{ ok: false, error: 'Not logged in or session has expired.' }` throws with `err.code === 'MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED'`; a 401 with `{ ok: false, error: 'Invalid master password', code: 'INVALID_PASSWORD' }` and a 401 with `{ ok: false, error: 'Invalid current password' }` throw without that code.

success_criteria.criterion: At a terminal, a rejected token is deleted and the device flow runs; elsewhere the token stays and the message names `mc vault status`.
success_criteria.check: `tests/vault/engine/vault-commands.test.js`: with a portal whose `memoroFetch` throws `MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED`, `isTty: true` deletes the token account through the injected `deleteSecret` and calls the injected device flow once with the configured `apiUrl`, exit code 1; `isTty: false`, `--json`, and `MEMORO_TOKEN` set each call neither, keep the token, and print (or emit as JSON with `code: 'MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED'`) a message containing `mc vault status`.

success_criteria.criterion: No sign-in hint names a command that does not exist.
success_criteria.check: `git grep -nE 'memoro-cli login|run .mc setup.|Run .mc. to sign in' src tests` prints nothing.

steps.title: The vault key cache writes on macOS again
steps.done_when: `cacheVaultKey` returns true through the real `macSet` guard, the entry reads back with the same key bytes, and a pre-2026-10-10 plain-JSON entry still reads.
instruction: The fault: `cacheVaultKey` (`src/vault/engine/key-cache.js`) stores `JSON.stringify({ vaultKeyB64, authHash?, deviceId?, expiresAt })` through `setSecret` (`src/lib/keychain.js`). Since b9c9fff8 (#843, 2026-10-10) `macSet` refuses any value containing `"`, `\`, `\r` or `\n` with `EBADSECRET`, and `setSecret` rethrows `EBADSECRET` rather than falling back to the file. A JSON value always contains quotes, so on macOS every write fails; `cacheVaultKey` catches it and returns `false`, and `mc vault unlock` prints "the local key cache could not be written". Every process after that prompts for the master password, and a headless one cannot read the vault at all.

The fix lives in `key-cache.js` only. Add a module-private prefix `const CACHE_PREFIX = 'b64:';` and an encoder: the value written is `CACHE_PREFIX + Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(record), 'utf8').toString('base64')`. Base64's alphabet and `:` are all accepted by `macSet`. Use it in `cacheVaultKey`; the record's fields and the best-effort `try/catch` returning `false` stay as they are.

Reading: `parseCacheRecord(raw, now)` is the one parser — `readCachedVaultKey` and `inspectCachedVaultKey` both go through it. At its top, when `raw` starts with `CACHE_PREFIX`, decode the remainder (`Buffer.from(rest, 'base64').toString('utf8')`) and `JSON.parse` that; otherwise `JSON.parse(raw)` as today, which is the pre-2026-10-10 shape and must keep working. Any failure in either path returns the existing `{ present: false, …, reason: 'invalid-json', clear: true }`. Node's base64 decoder does not throw on junk, so a non-base64 remainder surfaces as a `JSON.parse` failure — that is the path to rely on, not a decoder exception.
Update the module's header comment: the cache value is the record above, base64-encoded behind `b64:`, because `macSet` cannot carry a JSON string; plain JSON is still read. Name `macSet` and #843.

Tests, in `tests/vault/engine/key-cache.test.js` (it already has an in-memory `makeMemDeps`; its `setSecret` accepts anything, which is why #843 passed — that is the gap). Add: (1) a round trip whose `deps.setSecret` is `(account, value) => macSet(account, value, { exec })` with `exec` capturing the stdin string, and whose `deps.getSecret` returns the `-w "…"` value parsed out of that line; write a durable entry with `authHash` and `deviceId` and assert `true`, same bytes, `durable === true`, both fields back. Import `macSet` from `src/lib/keychain.js` as `tests/lib/keychain.test.js` does. (2) A store seeded directly with plain JSON in the old shape reads as present and is not deleted. (3) `b64:` + `'%%%'` and `b64:` + base64 of `'not json'` both read as `null`, are deleted, and `inspectCachedVaultKey` says `invalid-json`. Existing tests that assert on the stored string's shape, if any, change to decode it.
Run `npm test` (`node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs 'tests/**/*.test.js'`). Land with `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: A rejected Memoro token signs in again at a terminal, and sign-in hints name what works
steps.done_when: A token rejection from Memoro carries `MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED`; `mc vault` deletes the token and runs the device flow at a terminal and otherwise names `mc vault status`; no hint names `memoro-cli login`, `mc setup` or bare `mc` as the way to sign in.
instruction: How it fails today: `memoroFetch` (`src/lib/api.js`) throws `Memoro 401: <error>` with `err.status = 401` and `err.data` for any non-2xx (`parseMemoroResponse`). `mc vault`'s `run()` (`src/cli/vault.js` ~113–135) catches it and prints `mc vault: Memoro 401: Not logged in or session has expired.` The device flow only starts when *no* token is stored (`shouldTriggerDeviceFlow` / `needsDeviceAuth` in `src/lib/device-flow.js`, called from `main()` in `src/bin-mc.js` before the `vault` capability is dispatched); a stored token the server rejects counts as signed in. `mc auth memoro`, the old explicit path, went in #543. Device tokens live 90 days (memoro `src/routes/auth/device-flow.js`, `expiryDays: 90`), so every install meets this.

1 — Classify the rejection in `src/lib/api.js`. The server's token rejection is the generic body `{ ok: false, error: 'Not logged in or session has expired.' }` with no `code` (memoro `src/auth/session-guard.js` ~521, same text in `src/routes/boot.js` ~185). A plain status check is not enough: memoro's vault routes answer 401 themselves for a wrong password — `{ error: 'Invalid master password', code: 'INVALID_PASSWORD' }`, `{ error: 'Invalid current password' }` (no code), `{ error: 'Invalid recovery code', code: 'INVALID_RECOVERY' }` (memoro `src/routes/vault/index.js` ~388, ~524, ~612). Export `MEMORO_AUTH_REJECTED = 'Not logged in or session has expired.'` and, in `parseMemoroResponse`, set `err.code = 'MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED'` when `status === 401 && data?.error === MEMORO_AUTH_REJECTED && !data?.code`. The message and other fields stay. Also change the missing-token throw at the top of `memoroFetch` (`'Not logged in. Run \`memoro-cli login\` first.'`) to `'Not signed in to Memoro. Run \`mc vault status\` in a terminal to sign in.'`.

2 — Handle it in `run()` of `src/cli/vault.js`. In the `catch`, before the generic print, when `err?.code === 'MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED'` return `await handleRejectedToken(argv, opts)`. That function decides with the existing predicate rather than a new one: `shouldTriggerDeviceFlow({ hasToken: false, isTty: opts.isTty ?? process.stdout?.isTTY === true, mcTestMode: env.MC_TEST_MODE, memoroTokenEnv: env.MEMORO_TOKEN, argv: ['vault', ...argv] })` with `env = opts.env || process.env`, and additionally not when `argv` contains `--json`. The verb (`argv[0]`) is for the messages.

Interactive branch: print to stderr `Memoro rejected the stored sign-in (expired or revoked). Signing in again…`; delete the token with `deleteSecret(ACCOUNTS.TOKEN)` from `src/lib/keychain.js` (`ACCOUNTS` from `src/lib/auth-accounts.js`, as `loadPortal` already imports); run the device flow with `apiUrl = opts.portal?.apiUrl || getApiUrl([]) || (await readConfig()).apiUrl` — the same source as `loadPortal` (~1360–1371) — and `nextMessage: 'Next: run \`mc vault <verb>\` again.'` with the real verb. Return 1 whatever the flow returns: the verb itself did not run, and re-running it is the person's (as `bin-mc.js` already does after a fresh sign-in). Injection seams for tests, defaulting to the real ones: `opts.deleteToken`, `opts.deviceFlow`.

Other branch: leave the token. With `--json` emit `{ ok: false, error: 'Memoro rejected the stored sign-in (expired or revoked).', code: 'MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED' }`; otherwise print `mc vault: Memoro rejected the stored sign-in (expired or revoked). Sign in again by running \`mc vault status\` in a terminal.` Return 1. Use the file's existing `emit` helper so stderr/JSON behaviour matches the other errors.

3 — Hints that name a dead path. `src/cli/vault.js` `loadPortal` (~1368): `no Memoro token. Run \`mc\` to sign in first.` → `no Memoro token. Run \`mc vault status\` in a terminal to sign in.` (bare `mc` is the page, `src/mc/commands/home.js`, and never runs the device flow; only the `bin-mc.js` path does). `src/mc/first-run.js` `HINT_TEXT` (`New to mc? Run \`mc\` to sign in.`) → `New to mc? Run \`mc vault status\` to sign in.`, with `tests/mc/first-run.test.js` (~61). `src/lib/device-flow.js` `runDeviceFlow`'s default `nextMessage` (`Next: run \`mc setup\` to finish local setup.`, ~284) → `Next: run your command again.`, with `tests/lib/device-flow.test.js` (~375); and the comments at ~54 and ~64 that call `memoro-cli login` and `mc auth memoro` the explicit login paths say instead that there is no explicit login verb since #543 — `mc vault <verb>` at a terminal with no token is the sign-in. Leave the `OAUTH_STALE` block (~1335–1347) alone; it is out of scope.

Tests. `tests/lib/api.test.js` (`describe('memoro HTTP client')`): the three bodies in success criterion 3, through `memoroFetch` with an injected `fetchImpl`. `tests/vault/engine/vault-commands.test.js`: it already injects `opts.portal` with its own `memoroFetch` (see the `pure error paths` block ~657); make one throw an `Error` with `code = 'MEMORO_TOKEN_REJECTED'` and drive `['status']` with `isTty: true` (assert `deleteToken` called once, `deviceFlow` called once with the portal's `apiUrl` and a `nextMessage` naming `mc vault status`, return 1), with `isTty: false`, with `--json`, and with `env: { MEMORO_TOKEN: 'x' }` (assert neither called, return 1, output contains `mc vault status` or the JSON `code`).
Run `npm test`. Land with `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.
